glosses: A small, light vehicle with runners, used recreationally, mostly by children, for sliding down snow-covered hills; no draft animal pulls it.

examples.text: The child zoomed down the hill on his sled.

glosses: A vehicle on runners, used for conveying loads over the snow or ice, and often pulled by sled dogs.

examples.text: "Mush!" he yelled at the dogs pulling the sled.

glosses: A snowmobile.

examples.text: We saw them go by on their sleds this afternoon, headed toward their grandfather's quarter section.

glosses: A car (automobile) or truck, usually called so with the implication of sledlike traits: heavy, low-slung, and prone to going fast but not braking or cornering particularly well.

examples.text: Near-synonyms: land yacht, boat
He was a bit reckless and frankly we were nervous about riding with him in that big old sled of his, a Cadillac with a V-8.
That sled had manual drum brakes on all four corners.

glosses: To ride a sled.
To convey on a sled.

translations.source_sense_description: niedriger Sitz, der am vorderen Ende zwei nach oben gebogene Kufen hat

glosses: A heavy, long handled maul or hammer used to drive stakes, wedges, etc.

examples.text: [based on information from Major Hill, Master of the Silver Mills, in 1662, describing silver mining in Cardiganshire] They dig the Oar thus; One holds a little Picque, or Punch of Iron, having a long Handle of Wood which they call a Gad; Another with a great Iron Hammer, or Sledge, drives it into the Vein.
Sledge hammers are only used for heavy-duty persuading when working on vehicles or machinery.

glosses: To hit with a sledgehammer.

examples.text: The rapid and violent exertion of smiths, mightily sledging the glowing iron masses of their furnaces.
When I inquired the reason of this wire being used in the construction of the safe, I was told it was to prevent the doors being broken by either sledging or wedging.

glosses: A low sled drawn by animals, typically on snow, ice or grass.

examples.text: The sledge ran far better upon the ice; I cannot say the same for the dogs.

glosses: any type of sled or sleigh.

examples.text: Aged wore out Coal-Horses, which after some time Wrought you will have, may serve turn for Sledge-Horses.

glosses: A card game resembling all fours and seven-up; old sledge.
To drag or draw a sledge.

examples.text: It should be remembered, that these explorations were nearly all made by our seamen and officers on foot, dragging sledges, on which were piled tents, provision, fuel for cooking, and raiment. This sledging was brought to perfection by Captain M'Clintock.

glosses: To ride, travel with or transport in a sledge.

examples.text: He was also to initiate me in the American pastime of sleighing, or sledging.

glosses: To verbally insult or abuse an opponent in order to distract them (considered unsportsmanlike).

examples.text: I've never been one to sledge on the field. I was normally too tired to be bothered, but the one time I did, didn't I cop it.

glosses: To (cause to) move in continuous contact with a surface.

examples.text: He slid the boat across the grass.
The safe slid slowly.
Snow slides down the side of a mountain.

glosses: To move on a low-friction surface.

examples.text: The car slid on the ice.
They bathe in summer, and in winter slide.

glosses: To drop down and skid into a base.

examples.text: Jones slid into second.

glosses: To lose one’s balance on a slippery surface.

examples.text: He slid while going around the corner.

glosses: To pass or put imperceptibly; to slip.

examples.text: to alter the meaning of a question by sliding in a word
Schoolchildren sometimes slide each other notes during class.

Lachey and Olson have become rather chummy the last couple of years—they slide each other free tickets, they visit each other at practice sessions and games, their wives hang out—and, well, Olson has been filling Lachey’s head with a lot of baseball talk.

glosses: To subtly direct a facial expression at (someone).

examples.text: He slid me a dirty look.

glosses: To pass inadvertently.

examples.text: Beware thou ſlide not by it, leſt thou fall before him that lieth in wait.

glosses: To pass along smoothly or unobservedly; to move gently onward without friction or hindrance.

examples.text: A ship or boat slides through the water.
Ages shall slide away without perceiving.
Begin vvith Senſe, of ev'ry Art the Soul, / Parts anſw'ring parts ſhall ſlide into a VVhole, […]

All night no ruder air perplex
⁠Thy sliding keel, till Phosphor, bright
⁠As our pure love, thro’ early light
Shall glimmer on the dewy decks.

glosses: To decrease in amount or value.

examples.text: The stock market slid yesterday after major stocks released weak quarterly results.

glosses: To smoothly pass from one note to another by bending the pitch upwards or downwards.
To ride down snowy hills upon a toboggan or similar object for recreation.

glosses: To go; to move from one place or to another.

examples.text: "Gotta slide, this is my stop [on the train]."
